sermon.title: God's Correction Tactics Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “God’s Correction Tactics Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says God is slow to judge, yet he does involve himself in the lives of believers, correcting them because he loves them. He explains the difference between rebuke and chastening and how God speaks through parents, friends, the church, the Bible and civil authorities. He then presses the church to reach troubled homes and children, citing statistics on runaway youth.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Revelations 3:19” (Revelation 3:19). After reading Ecclesiastes 8:11 he continues with “though a sinner does evil a hundred times,” which is Ecclesiastes 8:12-13; the passage he attributes to Asaph and calls only “Psalms” is Psalm 73 (verse 17 is “the house of the Lord”). The caption “ASF” is read as Asaph. He cites United States Department of Health and Human Services figures on runaway youth without naming a report or year; they have not been checked here, and one figure is garbled in the captions (shown as [unclear]%). He names a politician and political parties, and mentions a family abuse case and child sexual exploitation; these are his own remarks and are kept as spoken. The captions garble a place name and a few other words, shown as [unclear] and not guessed.

chunks.section_question: Does God still judge and interfere in the affairs of people?
chunks.short_answer: He says that because God is slow to judge, people begin to think he does not judge or interfere in the affairs of men, and he points to Jeremiah 5:12 where the people say evil will not come on them. He says God’s words become fire to those who speak that way.
chunks.text: Because God is slow in judging a people, a nation, dealing with them, believers and unbelievers alike begin to think God does not judge nor interfere in the affairs of men. In fact, some of our founding fathers believe that that God does not involve himself in the affairs of men, and today they even mock at that statement. I’ve seen it on the Fox News and other news channels where they actually mock the idea of God doing anything to punish people for sin. In Jeremiah 5:12 it says, they have lied about the Lord. They said it is not he, neither will evil come upon us, nor shall we see sword or famine. The prophets, the preachers, are but wind.

chunks.section_question: Why do wicked people seem to get away with sin?
chunks.short_answer: He says that when sin is not corrected quickly, evil becomes the new norm, and that a sinner who never repents can seem blessed. He tells listeners not to compare themselves to the sinner who seems to get away with it, because God has saved such people for the end time destruction, and those who fear God will have it well.
chunks.text:
Ecclesiastes 8:11, if the sentence against evil, or those that do evil, is not executed speedily, the heart of men is fully set in them to do evil. You see, if there is no correction, then what we’re doing becomes the new norm, the new law. Though a sinner, now listen to this, this is a powerful statement, though a sinner, a flagrant sinner, doesn’t repent, never repents, though he does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged, and as it says in Psalms, nothing happens to his herds, nothing happens to his flock, he never gets sick, uh, you know, everything just seems to be working right for him. Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are prolonged, and his life seems to be blessed, yet I surely know that it will be well with those who fear God. Isn’t that beautiful?

You see, don’t compare yourself to the sinner out there that seems to be getting away with it. Because if you know the Scriptures in Psalms, Asaph said, I, Lord, I, I don’t understand why these evil people are just seemingly nothing bad is happening to them, until he went into the house of the Lord. It says in Psalms, and then his eyes were open that God had saved them for the end time destruction. How many don’t want to be saved for the end time destruction? You’d rather God correct you now. Let me see, show God your hand: Lord, correct me now. I don’t want to be pushed aside and just inherit eternal fire. And so this is a very powerful statement. So do not measure yourself by unbelievers, but realize what is the fear of the Lord: to depart from evil. If I live a life of righteousness, M, repent when I do things wrong, God is going to do good to me and going to do well for me, and in my in days I’ll look back on a blessed life. Amen, hallelujah. Very powerful.

chunks.section_question: What is the difference between God rebuking and chastening us?
chunks.short_answer: He says rebuke is verbal, telling a fault to convince, and God comes verbally first. Chasten means to train up and educate by discipline or punishment. He says God’s Word can correct us so that we do not need to be punished.
chunks.text:
Now, rebuke. He says, I rebuke. Rebuke is to tell a fault, to convince. So the first source of his correction is to verbally come and say you’re messing up. He’s going to verb... that’s what parents do. Son, you can’t do that. You cannot stick your finger in an electric socket. It’s going to straighten your hair. It’s going to knock you 15 feet. It’s verbal. Son, you cannot go out and play in the street. The cars are going to smash you. You know, it’s verbal. And so God comes, comes verbally first. How many are glad of that? Yeah. How many would like a hearing ear to hear God verbally? Yeah, yeah.

And then he says, I will chasten, I will correct you. The word chasten is to train up, educate by discipline or punishment. Let me say it again. Chasten here is different than rebuke. Rebuke is verbal. Chasten is to train up and educate by discipline, by punishment. Say I do something that makes your life uncomfortable, and then you will straighten up. So in this verse we see there are two ways God corrects his people, besides, as we taught last week, our sin corrects us and our backslidings correct, correct us. Here God gets involved and corrects us verbally. He tells us we’re wrong, and this is why we need to assemble in Bible studies and, and church. Uh, we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation, and we need to go for the Word, because his Word will correct us. And I would rather be corrected by the Word of God than having him to come and punish me in some way, amen, because when God punish me, it also has a tendency to affect other members of my family or those around me. So it’d be better just to listen to the Word.

chunks.section_question: How does the Lord take up children whose parents forsake them?
chunks.short_answer: He says the Lord takes them up through the church: the church gets the message out to children, brings them in, and teaches them what is right and wrong. He tells of a time he dealt with two sisters, where the one who took her children to church had children who knew what was wrong.
chunks.text:
But the Bible says in Psalms 27:10, when my parents forsake me, when they turn their back on me, the Lord will take me up. Now, how does the Lord take them up? The parent, the church. See, the church has got to wake up to what it really is. You know, we are here to get the message out that there’s a better way to live, and we’re here to get the message out to children that there’s a better way to live. And so when the children hear, they come to church, you go out and you bring them in, and they come to church and they hear what is right and wrong, and then they go home and they know something’s wrong here. chunks.section_question: What does he say about runaway youth in America?
chunks.short_answer: He says the church used to speak out on righteousness and sin but now offers psychology and feel-good messages. He cites figures on teenage runaways being abused and says 1.6 million young people 18 and under run away every year in America.
chunks.text: In the ‘90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice, but after the ‘90s you don’t hear the church speaking out on righteousness and sin. You hear psychology and feel-good messages, and God, you know, want you, you self-esteem, God wants you to have self-esteem. Well, my, you know, come on, church, we need the teaching of God’s Word, amen, in right and wrong. The United States Department of Health and Human Services said 46% of teenage runaways 18 and under are physically abused, [unclear]% were sexually abused, that’s why they ran away, 38% was emotionally abused: you’re no good, you’re worth, you’ll never amount to anything, uh, no interaction, the kid just left alone. 60%, 66% of runaways had an alcohol parent, two-thirds of runaways were running from alcohol and the abuse and the problems that come with it. 25% are running from those parents who abuse drugs. That’s 91% of runaways in America, or throwaways, are drug and alcohol related. Are you there? And the church wants to argue about whether Jesus drank or didn’t drink. Folks, there’s something wrong in America. Now listen. You say, well, so what? Well, there’s 1.6 million 18 and under running away every year in America.

chunks.section_question: Where is the church when young people are on the streets?
chunks.short_answer: He asks whether the church cares or only wants to enjoy the presence of God, and says no one is addressing the problem. He says these young people are exposed to sex trafficking and survival sex, and says the church is silent.
chunks.text:
In 10 years that’s 16 million. Obama never addresses it, the Democrats never address it, the Republicans aren’t addressing it, no one is addressing it, and the church is silent. And yet we worry about the war in Iraq, and we worry about the border, and we worry about all a lot of these things, abortion and so forth, and yet 1.6 million of our young people are out on the streets every year. Does the church care, or do we just want to come in and enjoy the presence of God and hear an inspirational message and hear about us sending mission money to the mission field and feeding the [unclear] down here and the [unclear] that drops out and [unclear] and everything we are? Where is the church in this thing?

These kids are exposed to sex trafficking. They’re actually being sold for sex, sex for survival. They have sex just so somebody will give them a roof to be under and some food. And we’re talking about kids from 10, 11 up to 18 years old. One mother sold her own child for sex in South Carolina. All this sexual promotion in America, and if it feels good, do it. The mentality is, you know, sex is the thing, and sex is okay, and we, and we sell our kids. There’s some wrong when a mother who has a God-given protection button in her, you touch that kid, man, you just caught a tail of a wild cat, and that is changed and neutralized to where have my daughter, have my son, give me a hundred bucks. Are you there? And what is the church saying? We’re saying nothing. Either they get HIV and they get viral diseases and they go into prostitution, and it’s just embarrassing. It’s shameful what is happening to 1.6 million youth every year. And some of these kids are thrown out by their parent. They don’t want them anymore, they’re just in the way, and other ones are running away.

chunks.section_question: What does he say is the source of America’s problems?
chunks.short_answer: He says the source of America’s problems right now is the home, and that no one is addressing it. He says the church is here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and to comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.
chunks.text: Matthew 10:36, Jesus said, a man’s enemies will be those of his own household, and that is exactly what’s happening in America. The source of America’s problems right now is the home, and no one is addressing it, and the church, in my research, including this one, has not stood up publicly and declared that this is wrong. What politician running for office hammers about these issues? None. See, they want the right for women to have abortion, they’ll hammer, you know, environmental issues, they hammer all kinds of things, and no one is going to the rescue of these innocent kids being thrown out or running away from abusive homes. The church is there. We are here. We’re not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but we’re here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage [unclear] neglected children, neglected youth, and we should be going out of our way to do that. We should have time to do that. Can I hear an amen?

chunks.section_question: How can a church work together as a team?
chunks.short_answer: Using a football team as his picture, he says every player must know the role, the part and the goal, and that the church must agree to work as a team to get the Word of God out to homes and children. He says it is nothing for God to save by many or by few.
chunks.text: You see, to do that we got to become a team. They’ve been talking about teams on Friday, you got to join the team. We’re having Super Bowl today, and every player has to play as this team player. They got to know their role, they got to know their part, they got to know the goal. The goal is to get that football in the end zone, and whatever it takes to get it there, we got to work as a team to do it. We got to protect our quarterback, we got to block for our runner. Are you there? The quarterback can’t go out there and hack the ball to himself and then throw it to himself. And church, look at you. You can decide today to be a team, because the Bible says it’s nothing for God to say by many or by few. But the key is we got to agree to work as a team and set a goal to get the Word of God out to these homes and get these, the Word out to these children and bring them in. That bus should be full of kids, because in no area have I been that there is such a high percentage of troubled homes in [unclear]. And I’ve ministered in a lot of areas in California. There’s a lot of troubled homes out there, messed up homes, parents who don’t know what they’re doing, they’re just self-centered, selfish, and accidentally had kids.

chunks.section_question: How can a friend correct us, and what about bad friends?
chunks.short_answer: He says a good friend will correct you when you are wrong, and a Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend who seduces you into things against God’s word will lead you astray.
chunks.text: Now then, we got the friend, a friend, a close acquaintance, they can correct us. A man sharpens the countenance of his friend, Proverbs 27:17. See, as iron sharpens iron, we sharpen the countenance, the conscience, see, the person of our friend, and a good friend will do that. A good friend will correct you when you’re wrong. But what if that friend is not a good friend? Psalms 41:9, my own familiar friend in whom I trust, who ate my bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me. And a lot of your acquaintances are trying to lure you and seduce you into doing things that are against God’s word. We don’t have to go to church, it’s okay to drink and [unclear], they are seducing it. These kind of friends aren’t Bible friends. A Bible friend will verbally correct you. A worldly friend will lead you astray.

faqs.question: What does Jeremiah 5 say God will not do?
faqs.answer: In the passage he reads, God says that even in those days of judgment, “I will not destroy you completely.” He says that is because God’s ultimate plan is to restore.

scriptures.text_nkjv: They have lied about the LORD, And said, “It is not He. Neither will evil come upon us, Nor shall we see sword or famine. And the prophets become wind, For the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them.” Therefore thus says the LORD God of hosts: “Because you speak this word, Behold, I will make My words in your mouth fire, And this people wood, And it shall devour them. Behold, I will bring a nation against you from afar, O house of Israel,” says the LORD. “It is a mighty nation, It is an ancient nation, A nation whose language you do not know, Nor can you understand what they say. Their quiver is like an open tomb; They are all mighty men. And they shall eat up your harvest and your bread, Which your sons and daughters should eat. They shall eat up your flocks and your herds; They shall eat up your vines and your fig trees; They shall destroy your fortified cities, In which you trust, with the sword. “Nevertheless in those days,” says the LORD, “I will not make a complete end of you.

faqs.question: What is the goal of God’s correction?
faqs.answer: He says God’s ultimate plan is to restore, and that God corrects so that we can go on, just as a parent corrects the problem rather than throwing the child out.

faqs.question: Should we measure ourselves by unbelievers?
faqs.answer: He says no: do not measure yourself by unbelievers, but realize the fear of the Lord is to depart from evil. He says if we live a life of righteousness and repent when we do wrong, God will do good to us.

faqs.question: Why do a husband and wife correct each other?
faqs.answer: He says a husband and wife correct each other because they love each other and want the marriage and the family to be strong.

faqs.question: What two ways of correction does he find in Revelation 3:19?
faqs.answer: He says that in this verse there are two ways God corrects his people: rebuke, which is verbal, and chastening, which is to train up and educate by discipline or punishment.

scriptures.text_nkjv: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten. Therefore be zealous and repent.

faqs.question: Why would he rather be corrected by God’s Word than by punishment?
faqs.answer: He says he would rather be corrected by the Word of God than have God punish him, because when God punishes, it also has a tendency to affect other members of his family or those around him.

faqs.question: What does he say we need instead of miracles, flattering prophecies and tongues?
faqs.answer: He says we need to forget about the miracles and the flattering prophecies and the tongues and interpretation and go for the Word, because his Word will correct us.

faqs.question: What does he say about depression and correction?
faqs.answer: He says King Saul had a depressed, angry spirit come upon him because of his sins and God was correcting him. He says he knows Christians who are depressed all the time and recommends that we recognize the problem, get it solved and move on.

faqs.question: Does God speak to us with an audible voice from heaven?
faqs.answer: He says it is not going to be an audible voice from heaven. He says God will come and use people to correct us verbally.

faqs.question: What does he say about parents and grown children?
faqs.answer: He says even a grown-up child may need verbal correction or advice from a parent, but that some parents never let their kids grow up.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well pleasing to the Lord.

faqs.question: What does he say about the church speaking out in America?
faqs.answer: He says that in the ’90s the church spoke out openly for righteousness and justice but after that you hear psychology and feel-good messages. He says the church needs the teaching of God’s Word in right and wrong.

faqs.answer: He says we are not just people here to come in and sing songs and enjoy the blessings of God, but are here to be a source to straighten out troubled homes and comfort and encourage neglected children and youth.

faqs.answer: He says a Bible friend will verbally correct you, while a worldly friend will lead you astray.
